start.meta.title: Gregor Zwanzig – Weather briefing for hikes
start.meta.description: Gregor Zwanzig delivers a hyperlocal weather forecast for your stage points and locations – as a briefing by email or Telegram, plus alerts.
start.hero.title: The weather for your stage, right where you are.
start.hero.lead: Gregor Zwanzig sends you the weather for your trips as a compact briefing – by email as the main channel, and additionally by Telegram if you like.
start.was.title: What is Gregor Zwanzig?
start.was.text: Gregor Zwanzig is a weather service for people who walk for several days, for example on the GR20. You create a trip with its stages or compare several locations in a location comparison. Gregor fetches the forecasts, evaluates them and sums them up in short, readable briefings.
start.was.hyperlokal: You get a hyperlocal forecast: for the stage points of your trip during the trip period, or for the locations of your location comparison – as a briefing in the morning and in the evening, plus alerts when the weather changes in a way that matters to you.
start.ankommt.title: What you receive
start.ankommt.briefing: A briefing every morning and evening with the weather for the next hours and stage sections – clearly laid out as a table in the email or compact as a Telegram message.
start.ankommt.alarm: Alerts come in between briefings when thunderstorms, heavy rain, wind or other hazards approach your route.
start.ankommt.kanaele: Email is the main channel, Telegram is optional. Messages by SMS or satellite messenger with a return channel are in progress or available on request.
start.nutzen.title: Why this helps on the trail
start.nutzen.empfang: On the trail you cannot predict what gets through: at the hut you are more likely to have Wi-Fi, on the pass normal mobile reception. That is why every channel answers every question – with the same content, only in the form that suits the channel.
start.nutzen.entscheidung: So at breakfast you can already decide whether to set off, start earlier or plan a stage differently – without reading weather maps yourself.
